stem: Which type of AI creates new content, such as text, images or code, in response to a prompt?

options.text: Predictive analytics
Rule-based expert system
Generative AI
Robotic process automation

explanation: Generative AI produces new content from patterns it learned in training. Predictive analytics forecasts values, a rule-based expert system applies fixed if-then rules, and RPA repeats scripted user-interface steps without creating anything new.

stem: What is a large language model (LLM)?

options.text: A neural network trained on huge text corpora to predict the next token
A relational database that stores dictionary terms for later search queries
A rules engine that checks spelling and grammar against a fixed word list
A dashboard feature that turns spoken questions into report chart filters

explanation: An LLM is a deep neural network trained on huge volumes of text to predict the next token, which lets it generate language. It is not a database, a fixed rules engine or a dashboard feature.

stem: Which term describes a large model pretrained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks?

options.text: Decision tree
Data mart
Lookup table
Foundation model

explanation: A foundation (foundational) model is pretrained on broad data at scale and then adapted through prompting or fine-tuning. A decision tree is a single narrow model, a data mart is a subject-specific store, and a lookup table only maps fixed values.

stem: Which branch of machine learning uses neural networks with many layers to learn features from raw data?

options.text: Linear regression
Deep learning
Association rules
Decision trees

explanation: Deep learning stacks many neural network layers so the model learns its own features from raw inputs such as pixels or text. Linear regression fits a single equation, association rules find co-occurring items, and decision trees split data with a sequence of feature rules.

stem: Which field of AI focuses on enabling computers to interpret and generate human language?

options.text: Computer vision
Robotic process automation
Natural language processing
Optical character recognition

explanation: NLP covers tasks such as tokenizing, classifying, translating and generating text. Computer vision works with images, RPA automates clicks and keystrokes, and optical character recognition only converts images of text into characters.

stem: What does robotic process automation (RPA) do?

options.text: Uses software bots to repeat rule-based tasks across applications
Uses physical robots to move stock around a warehouse floor
Trains neural networks to recognize objects in camera images
Generates new report narratives from a short written prompt

explanation: RPA bots mimic the clicks and keystrokes a person would make to complete repetitive, rule-based work. It does not involve physical robots, image recognition models or generative text.

stem: Every Monday an analyst logs in to three portals, downloads CSV exports, pastes them into a template and emails the result. Which technology best automates this report with no change to the source systems?

options.text: A large language model
A deep learning classifier
A computer vision model
Robotic process automation

explanation: RPA bots can log in, download files, update a template and send email by following the same scripted steps through the existing user interface. An LLM, a classifier or a vision model predicts or generates content but does not drive the portals and files on its own.

stem: A support team wants to tag thousands of free-text customer comments as positive, neutral or negative. Which AI technique fits this task?

options.text: Robotic process automation
Sentiment analysis with NLP
Time series forecasting
K-means clustering on order totals

explanation: Sentiment analysis is an NLP task that classifies the tone of text. RPA repeats fixed steps and cannot judge tone, forecasting predicts future values, and clustering order totals ignores the comment text entirely.

stem: An analyst asks a chatbot to summarize a sales report, and the summary cites a regional figure that does not appear anywhere in the data. What is this behavior called?

options.text: Overfitting
Data drift
Hallucination
Tokenization

explanation: A hallucination is fluent, confident output from a generative model that is not supported by its input or by facts. Overfitting is a training problem, data drift is a change in input data over time, and tokenization just splits text into units.

stem: A company adapts a pretrained foundation model by training it further on its own labeled support tickets. What is this process called?

options.text: Fine-tuning
Normalization
Pretraining
Prompt chaining

explanation: Fine-tuning continues training a pretrained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset. Normalization rescales or restructures data, pretraining is the original broad training stage, and prompt chaining links prompts without changing the model weights.

stem: A business user types "show total revenue by region for last quarter" and the reporting tool returns a chart. Which AI concept makes this possible?

options.text: Robotic process automation
Image classification
Scheduled report bursting
Natural language query

explanation: A natural language query feature uses NLP to turn a plain-English question into a query and a visual. RPA replays fixed steps, image classification labels pictures, and report bursting splits and sends a finished report on a schedule.

stem: Why do LLMs need large amounts of computing power to train?

options.text: They store every training document in a searchable index
They learn billions of parameters from very large text datasets
They must check each output against a fixed set of rules
They rebuild the full model from scratch for every prompt

explanation: Training an LLM means adjusting billions of parameters across enormous text corpora, which needs large clusters of processors. The model does not store documents as an index, does not check rules, and is not rebuilt for each prompt.

stem: A team uses an LLM to write the narrative commentary for its monthly operations report. What is the most important control before the report is published?

options.text: Increase the length limit for the model output text
Run the same prompt twice and keep the longer text
Have an analyst verify each figure against the source
Convert the narrative to a locked file before sending

explanation: Generative output can contain plausible but wrong figures, so a person must check it against the source data. Longer output, repeated prompts or a different file format do nothing to confirm accuracy.

stem: A bank wants to read scanned loan forms, pull out the applicant details and key them into a legacy system that has no API. Which combination fits best?

options.text: Text recognition and NLP, then RPA to enter the values
Deep learning forecasting, then a scheduled SQL export job
An LLM to approve loans, then manual entry by staff
RPA alone to read the scanned images as plain text

explanation: Text recognition (optical character recognition) turns the scanned images into text, NLP pulls out the applicant fields, and RPA types them into a system with no API. Forecasting does not read forms, letting an LLM approve loans removes needed human judgment, and RPA alone cannot interpret images.

stem: An RPA bot that copies figures from a vendor portal into a weekly report suddenly starts failing after the vendor redesigns its web page. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The bot model has drifted because its training data is outdated
The bot needs a larger language model to read the new page layout
The bot has hallucinated values that the portal then rejected
The bot follows fixed screen steps that no longer match the page

explanation: Traditional RPA replays recorded, rule-based steps tied to screen elements, so a layout change breaks it. It is not a trained model, so drift, model size and hallucination do not explain the failure.

stem: A retailer must choose between training its own deep learning text model from scratch and adapting an existing foundation model. What is the main advantage of adapting the foundation model?

options.text: It keeps the model's knowledge up to date automatically
It needs much less labeled data and compute
It removes the need to review the outputs for bias
It lets the team skip evaluation of the model

explanation: A foundation model has already learned general patterns, so adapting it needs much less labeled data and training compute. It does not keep knowledge current, remove bias review or remove the need for evaluation.

stem: An analyst pastes customer records that contain PII into a public generative AI chatbot to get help cleaning them. What is the main concern?

options.text: The chatbot will reformat the columns in the records
The answers will take longer to generate
The data may leave the company and be kept by the provider
The records will be converted into an unstructured format

explanation: Sending PII to an outside AI service can breach privacy policy because the provider may store or reuse the prompt. Reformatted columns and slower answers are minor issues compared with data leaving the company, and a change to an unstructured format is not the issue either.

stem: Which TWO tasks are typical uses of generative AI for a data analyst?

options.text: Drafting a SQL query from a plain-English request
Writing a first-draft summary of a dashboard
Replicating a database to a standby server
Enforcing a primary key constraint on a table
Encrypting a file before it is transferred

explanation: Generative AI can draft SQL and summary text from prompts, which an analyst then checks. Key constraints, replication and encryption are database and security functions that do not generate content.

stem: Which TWO statements describe deep learning?

options.text: It relies on rules that a developer writes by hand
It is designed mainly for small structured tables
It usually needs large training datasets
It can learn features from raw images and text
It needs less training data than linear regression

explanation: Deep learning learns its own features from raw inputs such as images and text, and it generally needs large amounts of training data. It learns patterns rather than following hand-written rules, is not designed mainly for small structured tables, and needs more training data than linear regression, not less.

stem: Which TWO are common NLP tasks?

options.text: Outlier detection on sensor readings
Pivoting a sales table
Clicking through a web form
Machine translation
Named entity recognition

explanation: Entity recognition and translation both process human language. Outlier detection on sensor values is statistical, pivoting reshapes a table, and clicking through forms is RPA.

stem: Which TWO limitations should an analyst consider before relying on an LLM answer about company sales?

options.text: It returns the same answer to every rephrased question
It may state figures that are not in the source data
It reads the company database directly by default
Its knowledge stops at a training cutoff date
It refuses questions that contain numbers

explanation: LLMs can hallucinate figures and only know their training data up to a cutoff unless given current data. Their answers vary with wording, they do not read a company database unless connected to one, and they handle questions that contain numbers.

stem: Which TWO tasks are good candidates for RPA?

options.text: Interpreting why customer churn rose last quarter
Deciding which new market the company should enter next year
Copying invoice totals from emails into accounting software
Refreshing and exporting the same reports every morning
Designing a new data model for a recently merged business

explanation: RPA suits high-volume, repetitive, rule-based work such as data entry and scheduled report exports. Strategy decisions, causal interpretation and data model design need human judgment.

stem: Match each scenario to the AI concept it illustrates.

prompts.text: A chatbot drafts replies to customer emails
A vendor's general model is adapted to legal text
A bot keys invoice totals into accounting software
Support tickets are routed by the words they contain
A network learns to spot defects in product photos

explanation: Drafting replies is LLM text generation, adapting a broad pretrained model is a foundation model, keying values into software is RPA, routing by the words in text is NLP, and learning from photos is deep learning. The expert system is a distractor: none of these scenarios relies on rules written by hand.

partExplanations.p1: Generating reply text is the job of an LLM.
partExplanations.p2: A broadly pretrained model adapted to a domain is a foundation model.
partExplanations.p3: A bot repeating data entry steps in an application is RPA.
partExplanations.p4: Classifying tickets by their wording is NLP.
partExplanations.p5: Learning visual features from photos through many layers is deep learning.

stem: Sort each task into the technology best suited to it.

items.text: Draft a narrative summary of quarterly results
Download a portal export and email it every Friday
Create sample product descriptions from bullet points
Copy totals from one application into another nightly
Tag product names mentioned in reviews

explanation: Generative AI creates new text, RPA repeats fixed application steps, and NLP classification assigns labels to existing text.

partExplanations.i1: Writing a new summary is content generation.
partExplanations.i2: A fixed weekly download-and-send routine is RPA.
partExplanations.i3: Assigning topic labels to text is NLP classification.
partExplanations.i4: Producing new descriptions is content generation.
partExplanations.i5: Moving values between applications on a schedule is RPA.
partExplanations.i6: Labeling named entities in existing text is NLP classification.

stem: Put the stages of building a task-specific model from a foundation model into order.

steps.text: Deploy the model and monitor its outputs
Pretrain the model on a broad, general dataset
Evaluate the tuned model on held-out test data
Fine-tune the pretrained model on the labeled examples

explanation: A foundation model is pretrained first; the team then gathers labeled task data, fine-tunes, tests on unseen data and only then deploys with monitoring.

partExplanations.s1: Broad pretraining creates the foundation model.
partExplanations.s2: Task-specific labeled data is needed before tuning.
partExplanations.s3: Fine-tuning adapts the pretrained weights to the task.
partExplanations.s4: Held-out evaluation confirms the tuned model works.
partExplanations.s5: Deployment comes last, with monitoring for errors and drift.

stem: An analytics team uses the items shown. Select every item that is typically built with deep learning.
explanation: Large language models, image recognition and speech-to-text all rely on many-layered neural networks. Pivot tables, star schemas and lookup formulas are ordinary data tools with no learning.

partExplanations.s1: A large language model is built on deep neural networks.
partExplanations.s2: A pivot table is a standard data tool, not a learned model.
partExplanations.s3: An image recognition network is built on deep neural networks.
partExplanations.s4: A star schema is a standard data tool, not a learned model.
partExplanations.s5: A speech-to-text model is built on deep neural networks.
partExplanations.s6: A lookup formula is a standard data tool, not a learned model.

stem: An analyst needs to predict whether each customer will cancel a subscription next month (yes or no). Which model fits best?

options.text: Linear regression
A moving average
Logistic regression
ANOVA (Analysis of Variance)

explanation: Logistic regression predicts the probability of a yes/no outcome. Linear regression predicts a number on a continuous scale, and could give values below 0 or above 1.

stem: A logistic regression model returns 0.73 for one customer. What is that value?

options.text: The predicted probability that the outcome is yes
The customer's predicted spend in thousands
The correlation coefficient for the customer
The share of variation that the model explains

explanation: Logistic regression outputs a probability between 0 and 1. With the usual 0.5 threshold, 0.73 would be classed as "yes".
